highlights.title: OpenAI has a new $100 ChatGPT Pro plan to better match up with Claude
highlights.description: OpenAI has closed a yawning gap in its ChatGPT subscription pricing with a new $100 per month Pro plan that slots between the $20 per month Plus plan and $200 per month Pro plan. Offering five times more Codex than the $20 option, it appears designed to challenge Anthropic's $100 per month Claude option. "Compared with Claude Code, Codex delivers more coding capacity per dollar across paid tiers," an OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch. So what's the difference between OpenAI's two Pro plans? Th

highlights.title: OpenAI slams Anthropic in memo to shareholders as its leading AI rival gains momentum
highlights.description: OpenAI sent a memo to investors blasting chief rival Anthropic for "operating on a meaningfully smaller curve."

highlights.title: OpenAI Accuses Musk of ‘Ambush’ as $100 Billion-Plus Trial Looms
highlights.description: OpenAI says Elon Musk has suddenly changed direction on what he’s seeking in his lawsuit against the startup in a “legal ambush” just weeks before trial.

Anthropic Model Scare Sparks Urgent Bessent, Powell Warning to Bank CEOs
highlights.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell summoned Wall Street leaders to an urgent meeting on concerns that the latest artificial intelligence model from Anthropic PBC will usher in an era of greater cyber risk.

highlights.title: OpenAI says to update Mac apps including ChatGPT and Codex as security precaution
highlights.description: OpenAI is asking users of its Mac software to update to the latest releases from today “out of an abundance of caution.” This is due to a security issue with a third-party developer tool, Axios, that was used by OpenAI. more…

highlights.description: The ChatGPT-maker testified in favor of an Illinois bill that would limit when AI labs can be held liable—even in cases where their products cause “critical harm.”

ai.description: Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence company xAI sued Colorado to block a new state law requiring tech companies to establish safeguards to prevent discrimination by autonomous tools in certain employment decisions, among others.

ai.title: Gemini gets notebooks to help you organize projects
ai.description: Google's Gemini is getting a feature called "notebooks" to help you organize things about certain topics in a single place while using the AI chatbot, the company announced on Wednesday. You can pull in things like files, past conversations, and custom instructions into notebooks that Gemini can then use as context while you're talking with it. Notebooks sound a lot like ChatGPT's Projects feature, which launched in 2024 and similarly lets users store things about a certain topic in one spot. Go

ai.title: Google quietly launched an AI dictation app that works offline
ai.description: Google's new offline-first dictation app uses Gemma AI models to take on the apps like Wispr Flow.

ai.title: Arm CEO Says AI Is 'Much Bigger' Than the Internet Shift
ai.description: Arm CEO Rene Haas says the artificial intelligence boom is not just another tech cycle, but rather something "much bigger" and more far-reaching than anything that came before. In an interview with Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie, Haas explains why AI is scaling beyond the PC and mobile eras, driven by surging demand for compute, memory and infrastructure. This interview was recorded on March 23 for "Bloomberg Tech: Europe." (Source: Bloomberg)

ai.title: Zhipu Hikes Prices Again as China AI Monetization Wave Quickens
ai.description: Zhipu raised the cost of access to its most advanced AI model by at least 8%, joining other leading Chinese artificial intelligence players in trying to profit off years of research and computing investments.

other.title: Apple Hires Uber’s Asia-Pacific Government Relations Chief
other.description: Apple Inc. has hired Uber Technologies Inc.’s head of public policy and government relations for Asia-Pacific as it looks to revamp its supply chains in the region.

other.title: Philippines Asks Facebook to Curb Fake News, Warns of Legal Move
other.description: The Philippine government has asked Meta Platforms Inc., the parent company of Facebook, to implement measures to curb the spread of “false and panic-inducing content” on its platforms, warning of possible legal action if the company fails to act swiftly.

other.title: The Xiaomi 17 Ultra has some impressive add-ons that make snapping photos really fun
other.description: The Xiaomi 17 Ultra gives you a ton of options to play around with images, including preset filters and hardware add-ons.

other.title: Microsoft cuts cloudy desktop prices by 20 percent, warns they’ll wake up slowly
Microsoft hints at bit bunkers for war zones
China orders Apple to pull Dorsey's Bitchat, the messaging app used during Iran protests
other.description: The peer-to-peer app runs entirely over Bluetooth and mesh networks without an internet connection, making it popular with protesters and incompatible with Beijing's censorship regime.

other.title: Cryptographers place $5,000 bet whether quantum will matter
Men Are Buying Hacking Tools to Use Against Their Wives and Friends
other.description: In Telegram groups, men are sharing thousands of nonconsensual images of women and girls, buying spyware, and engaging in doxing and sexual abuse.

robotics.title: AI K-Pop Startup Galaxy Aims for IPO in Seoul, New York
robotics.description: Humanoid robots dressed in black, luxury hip-hop outfits snap into formation, moving in perfect sync to K-pop songs. It’s a simulation inside an office styled as a crash-landed spacecraft in the heart of Seoul’s financial district, complete with towering astronauts and floating robotic jellyfish.

robotics.title: Kia to Use Atlas Robots in US Plant, Develop First Software Car
robotics.description: Kia Corp. will begin using humanoid robots in its US factories from 2029 and is developing its first software-defined vehicle as the South Korean carmaker ramps up investment in new-generation cars and manufacturing technology to better compete with global rivals.

robotics.title: Robot Maker Kuka Eyes US, Asia as Europe’s Factories Lag on AI
robotics.description: Many of Europe’s industrial companies are too slow to adopt artificial intelligence, putting faster-moving global rivals in a position to overtake them, according to German-Chinese robotics maker Kuka AG.

business.title: Ackman’s Pershing Square Pitches Merger With Universal Music
business.description: Pershing Square Capital Management has proposed a combination with Universal Music Group NV that would move the listing into a US-based acquisition vehicle in a deal that Bill Ackman’s fund said will value the world’s biggest music label at a 78% premium to its last closing price.

business.title: Alibaba Leads $300 Million Bet on AI Video Platform ShengShu
business.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s cloud division led a 2 billion yuan ($293 million) funding round for ShengShu Technology, bolstering the war chest of a young contender in China’s crowded AI video contest.

business.title: SoftBank Group Prices ¥418 Billion Retail Bonds at Record 4.97%
business.description: SoftBank Group Corp. priced yen hybrid bonds targeting retail investors at an initial five-year coupon of 4.97%, marking the highest level for such debt issued by the company.

business.title: Arm CEO on Proposed California Wealth Tax: Not a Good Thing
business.description: Arm CEO Rene Haas warns a proposed wealth tax in California could drive top entrepreneurs out of Silicon Valley. "I don't think it's a good thing if it drives really smart people outside the valley," Haas tells Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie. This interview was recorded on March 23 for "Bloomberg Tech: Europe." (Source: Bloomberg)

business.title: AI Stocks in Asia Lure Back Global Funds as War Tensions Ease
business.description: As tensions in the Middle East begin to ease, global investors are turning their attention back to the artificial intelligence trade, funneling fresh funds into Asian tech stocks after weeks of selling.

business.title: Mythos AI threat prompts Bessent, Powell to convene bank CEOs for urgent talks
business.description: Mythos can rapidly spot software flaws and craft sophisticated exploits, raising fears of systemic risks in the banking system.

chips_cloud.title: China AI Firm Discloses $92 Million of Banned Nvidia Chip Servers to Beijing
chips_cloud.description: Hours after the United States charged a Super Micro Computer Inc. co-founder with illegally smuggling billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia Corp. AI chips to China, shares of a little-known Shenzhen-based computing company plummeted by the daily limit of 20%.

chips_cloud.title: TSMC’s Sales Beat Estimates After War Fails to Dent AI Demand
chips_cloud.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. reported a 35% increase in quarterly revenue, suggesting global AI chip demand remained intact during the first weeks of war in the Middle East.

chips_cloud.title: Bain Data Center Unit Cuts Ties With Nvidia Buyer After US Probe
chips_cloud.description: Bain Capital’s Bridge Data Centres has removed from its Malaysian computing hub a Southeast Asian company the US suspects of smuggling Nvidia Corp. chips.

chips_cloud.title: Samsung shares rise after profit seen jumping 8-fold on AI chip boom
chips_cloud.description: Samsung Electronics forecast record first-quarter operating profit that came in far above analyst estimates on booming demand for AI memory chips.

chips_cloud.title: Nvidia-Backed Lumentum Sees AI Filling Orders Through 2028
chips_cloud.description: Lumentum Holdings Inc. said demand from the biggest US tech companies for its optical components is accelerating and on track to fill its order books through 2028.

chips_cloud.title: Arm CEO Haas on Shifting From Smartphones to AI
chips_cloud.description: Arm CEO Rene Haas speaks to Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie as the chip company positions itself for a major shift beyond smartphones, betting big on the rapid growth of cloud computing and data centers. This interview was recorded on March 23 for "Bloomberg Tech: Europe." (Source: Bloomberg)

chips_cloud.title: AI Boom Driving $100 Bln Chip Opportunity, Arm CEO Says
chips_cloud.description: Chip company Arm is positioning itself for a major shift beyond smartphones, betting big on the rapid growth of cloud computing and data centers. CEO Rene Haas says the company expects this segment to dominate its business in the years ahead. Haas speaks to Bloomberg's Tom Mackenzie about the lucrative opportunity. This interview was recorded on March 23 for "Bloomberg Tech: Europe." (Source: Bloomberg)

chips_cloud.title: Japan Bets $16 Billion to Propel Startup Rapidus Into AI Chips
chips_cloud.description: Japan approved ¥631.5 billion ($4 billion) in additional subsidies to quicken Rapidus Corp. into the intensely competitive AI chipmaking arena, ramping up financial support for a signature project widely regarded as a long shot.

chips_cloud.title: S. Korea Posts Record Current Account Surplus on Chip Exports
chips_cloud.description: South Korea posted its biggest current account surplus on record in February as booming semiconductor exports lifted the goods balance before the Iran war began to ripple through energy markets and global shipping.

crypto.title: Attacking bitcoin mining with a quantum computer would require the energy of a star, academics say
crypto.description: One paper finds that attacking the bitcoin blockchain through quantum mining would demand the energy output of a star. Another replicates every major "quantum factoring breakthrough" using a 1981 home computer and a dog.

crypto.title: XRP may be less exposed to quantum computer threats than bitcoin, experts say
crypto.description: XRP’s design leaves a smaller share of its supply exposed to future quantum attacks than Bitcoin’s, experts said, pointing to additional XRPL features that stand out.

crypto.title: Circle future-proofs Arc blockchain against quantum threats
crypto.description: Circle’s Arc blockchain said users will be able to create wallets that withstand future quantum computer attacks from day one.

crypto.title: Quantum-safe bitcoin now possible without a soft fork, but costs $200 a pop, new research shows
crypto.description: A new scheme from a StarkWare researcher works under existing consensus rules, offering an emergency fallback while BIP-360 awaits activation.

crypto.title: Bitcoin gets its first working prototype of quantum-resistant wallet rescue tool
crypto.description: Lightning Labs CTO Olaoluwa Osuntokun demos a prototype that could prevent millions of wallets from being frozen under a future quantum-defense upgrade

space.title: The Moon is already on Google Maps—did Artemis II really tell us anything new?
space.description: "I think the biggest value here is the PR. I mean, it's getting the public excited."

space.title: Four astronauts are back home after a daring ride around the Moon
space.description: "I can't imagine a better crew that just completed a perfect mission right now."

space.description: Rocket's new AI platform combines strategy, product building, and competitive intelligence, aiming to move beyond code generation.

devices.description: Bloober Team announced today that its award-winning game Cronos: The New Dawn will launch on Apple silicon Macs with native support on April 28. Here are the details. more…

devices.description: A new report from IDC shows that while the overall PC market posted slight year-over-year shipment growth in the first quarter, Apple saw one of the strongest gains among its peers. Here are the details. more…

devices.title: Adobe’s low-processing camera app expands support to select iPads and the iPhone 17e
devices.description: The new update to Adobe’s experimental camera app adds initial support for iPads with at least 6GB of RAM and the new iPhone 17e. Here are the details. more…

devices.title: Apple Now Selling Parts for Seven New Devices Unveiled Last Month
devices.description: Launched in 2022, Apple's self-service repair program provides customers with access to genuine parts, tools, and manuals to repair select iPhones, iPads, Macs, Studio Displays, and Beats Pill speakers. Apple says the program is "intended for individuals who are experienced with the complexities of repairing electronic devices." devices.description: Apple has run into "more issues than expected" with its foldable iPhone that may set back its release, according to Nikkei. The engineering problems reportedly cropped up during the device's early test production phase and may delay first shipments by months, according to multiple sources briefed on the matter. devices.title: Google Pixel 10a finally launches in Japan with exclusive ‘Isai Blue’ color [Video]
devices.description: The Pixel 10a launched about a month ago in most of the world, but has been absent in Japan despite prior success for the Pixel in that region. That’s finally changing, though, as the Pixel 10a is now available for pre-order in Japan and, on top of that, it gets a special “Isai Blue” color that’s exclusive to the region. more…
